verdict.rationale: Post-Incident Reviews draw on the incident lifecycle, Slack data, and the Scribe Agent to build chronological incident narratives. Scribe also records key decisions, action items, and events from incident calls, which covers automatic capture of alerts, actions, and chat or call decisions. However, the evidence never explicitly documents an auto-captured incident timeline that SREs can edit or annotate afterwards. Editability is only implied by the PIR narrative-building workflow. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of an editable or annotatable timeline, detail on which alert and action events are auto-logged, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an SRE, the incident timeline is captured automatically — alerts, actions, and chat decisions — and I can edit or annotate it afterwards

citations.quote: Post-Incident Reviews integrate with your incident lifecycle, Slack data, and the PagerDuty Advance Scribe Agent to help your team uncover systemic patterns, build chronological incident narratives, and coordinate preventative follow-up actions
Schedule a Scribe Agent to join incident calls and record key decisions, action items, and events once a conference bridge is available.
Transcribe incident meetings in real time to enhance incident summaries and post-incident reviews
Teams can start PIRs directly from the incident detail page or Slack after resolving an incident
